gen-dafont-origami-gf-amiko: Unique from the first glance, Origami draws every letter in one brush stroke of constant width, lowercase dense as lead. Amiko's tall lowercase and outward-flicking terminals keep long paragraphs moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari opens its letter mouths wide and stands tall in the middle, a modern sans. Anek Devanagari then lets Origami, with its unmodulated strokes, make the noise while the text stays quiet.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-malayalam: Anek Malayalam reads clean and contemporary, its curves stopping short of touching and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase. And paragraphs of it move along easily beneath Origami, whose o is equally thick all round.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-telugu: Origami draws hollow, glass-tube lettering at constant thickness, stem to curve. Anek Telugu follows with wide, tall bowls and open, unlatched rounds that give clean, approachable text a rolling rhythm.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anuphan: Origami draws every letter like bent pipe, one constant stroke width, with lowercase heavy as poured lead type. Anuphan brings big round lowercase bowls and open curves with clear gaps that stay out of the way.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-arimo: Pen-plotter smooth, stubbornly single-stroke: that's Origami. Arimo, a sans with a tall mean line and spacious terminal gaps, gives that heading plain, sensible company down the page and lets it do the shouting.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-armata: One pen tip, one line width: Origami draws every letter that way. Armata, a sans-serif with spacious gaps and lowercase filling most of the letter height, is happy at small sizes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-carrois-gothic: Modern in tone, Carrois Gothic keeps generous curve openings and a high-set x-height, while Origami draws everything with one unchanging pen. One shouts in constant lines, the other quietly gets on with the reading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Contemporary through and through, Origami draws every letter with a single constant line width. Carrois Gothic SC, with clear openings at every curve end and capitals nearly lowercase height, reads smoothly across pages.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-chocolate-classica: Origami draws each stroke with one fixed nib, lowercase dense as poured lead type. Chocolate Classical Sans, a modern sans-serif with a sizable lowercase and broad-nibbed strokes that never curl shut, keeps paragraphs inviting.
